name: agent-harness-marketplace
description: Modules that install natively on Claude Code, pi and dsh from one content tree.

plugins.name: plan-for-dummies
plugins.description: Write an implementation plan that a less capable model (Sonnet, Haiku, a cheap subagent) will execute without the planner present.

plugins.name: ste-writing
plugins.description: Write prose in a controlled style modeled on ASD-STE100 (Simplified Technical English) at about 80% strictness, only when the user asks for it.

plugins.name: dual-agent-pr-review
plugins.description: Review a GitHub PR with Claude Code and Codex in parallel, then reconcile their findings into one consensus set.

plugins.name: agent-transcripts
plugins.description: Export Claude Code, pi and dsh transcripts into one on-device cache and index them in a derived sqlite database.

plugins.name: pr-flow
plugins.description: Work off main on every harness: branch + worktree, PR, watch CI until green, merge only when told, tear down after merge.

plugins.name: local-workers
plugins.description: Explicitly requested delegation to self-hosted models: the pi agent through the pi-run script (resumable, forkable sessions), the d3-ultra decision model for batched yes/no, choice and score questions, a mixed local+cloud fleet skill, and a replay benchmark against merged fixes

plugins.name: browser
plugins.description: Drive a browser from any harness: headless auto mode, headed hybrid mode where a human logs in and the agent takes over, or attach to a browser the user opened via its debug port — through agent-browser on a persistent per-identity profile.

plugins.name: feature-dev
plugins.description: Guided seven-phase feature development: explore the codebase with parallel specialist agents, ask clarifying questions, compare architectures, implement, then review. A harness-neutral port of Anthropic's feature-dev plugin whose agents dispatch on Claude Code, pi and dsh.

plugins.name: code-review
plugins.description: Automated pull-request review on every harness: a size gate sends a small or generated-only change to one combined reviewer, everything else to a five-lens fan-out plus batch scoring; anything under 80 is dropped, one comment posted with gh.

plugins.name: best-practices
plugins.description: Library of domain best-practices skills with stable, citable rule IDs (containers, uv, Python, FastAPI, databases, repo hygiene, Go, gRPC, QNAP QPKG packaging, Claude Code configuration and prompts) plus the containers-audit interactive scan-and-fix workflow and the authoring tools for adding rules.

plugins.name: best-practices-maintainer
plugins.description: Maintainer tooling for the best-practices library: rebuild the uv rule set from uv's own docs at a pinned release with a multi-agent extract, judge and live-check workflow.

plugins.name: okf-wiki
plugins.description: A per-repo, self-healing agent wiki in Open Knowledge Format: a session-start digest, background capture and re-verification on cheap models, and a reflect loop that measures whether it helps.

plugins.name: edit-lint
plugins.description: After every edit, run the linter that fits the file (shellcheck, actionlint, kubeconform, ansible-lint, node --check, tsc) and feed its findings back to the agent.

plugins.name: sleep-guard
plugins.description: Block a Bash call that opens with a foreground sleep of 5s or more and point the agent at a condition wait or a background job instead.

plugins.name: artifacts
plugins.description: Local HTML artifacts for pi and dsh: Claude's artifact design, dataviz and diagramming craft plus a stdlib check-and-deliver helper; one self-contained file, no hosting.

plugins.name: switchboard
plugins.description: Coordination for concurrent agent sessions (Claude Code, pi, dsh) on one machine: who is doing what, threaded messages between sessions, a todo board, a ledger of shared-state changes, and enforced leases on shared resources.

plugins.name: repo-sweep
plugins.description: Whole-repository review sweep on any harness: split the repo into parts, fan out finders over five lenses, prove every finding, track each one in a ledger across runs, and (on request) open fix pull requests.
